- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., 0.33 or below), model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 1.00 or 0.67 recurring), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 3–8% to offset overconfidence.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope or apply mean reversion to prior 5–7 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate in bearish sentiment cycles; add 1–3% to forecast to account for downward momentum lag.
- If recent history shows high volatility with alternating sentiment, model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast using 3–5 day moving average.
